# Fixed: Match imported files whose artist tag lists several artists or holds a web address

Part of the [custom Lidarr image](https://github.com/chodeus/Lidarr/tree/custom) (`ghcr.io/chodeus/lidarr:custom`), which merges this branch into `develop`. It is stacked on `feat/artist-alias-distance` and merges after it. Reviewed in [#56](https://github.com/chodeus/Lidarr/pull/56).

Import identification scores the files' artist tag, the album artist where there is one, as a single name against the release artist. Artist carries the heaviest weight in the album distance. A tag that names the album artist alongside others, such as "Artist A;Artist B" or "Artist A feat. Artist B", took a large artist penalty. A web address that a download site wrote into the album artist tag took the full penalty. Either could leave a correct release short of the import threshold.

- The tag's whole text is scored against the artist's name and aliases as before. A tag that credits several artists, split at `;`, `/`, `,` and `&`, is also scored artist by artist, and the closest one counts with a fixed penalty of 0.2 on top. That penalty keeps a match on one listed artist below a near miss on the whole credit, such as a missing "The", so a release by one of them can't outrank the release credited to all of them. The whole credit is also scored with "&" read as "and" on both sides, which matters most for short names, and the lower score counts; that reading carries 0.01, so the credit as written still ranks ahead of a different artist spelled with "and". A correct release never scores worse than before, and gains whenever the whole tag missed by more than that penalty.
- Guests after "feat.", "ft." or "featuring" are left out, with or without a bracket or a space before them, so "Artist A feat. Artist B" and "Artist A (feat. Artist B & Artist C)" count toward Artist A only. A guest has to start with a word after the dot or space, so a name that ends in "Feat", alone or followed by ";", "/" or ",", is left whole.
- A credit in another order than the release's, "Artist B & Artist A" against "Artist A & Artist B", still ranks one of its artists first, as on `develop`.
- An artist tag that is entirely a web address (a scheme such as `https://`, a `www.` prefix, or a single word ending in `.com`, `.net`, `.org`, `.info`, `.biz`, `.ru` or `.io`) isn't scored, as for Various Artists releases. A name followed by an address, or a dotted name like "d.j.name", is scored as before.
- `Distance.AddStringToClosest` from `feat/artist-alias-distance` becomes `Distance.ClosestPenalty`, which returns the penalty so the two scores can be compared.

Tests: a tag crediting several artists scores closer than the same text as one name, and closer than an unrelated artist; the whole credit outranks one of its artists, including "&" against "and", a missing "The" and a listed name ending in "Feat"; the credit as written outranks its "and" spelling; a name written without its "&" still matches; the main artist outranks a featured guest, bracketed or not; names that contain a separator match themselves; a list naming neither artist, an empty tag and dotted names are still penalised; web addresses, padded or not, aren't scored, and a name followed by one still is. Thirteen mutations each fail a test, among them a penalty of 0.1 on a listed artist, guests kept, both earlier guest patterns, no tie-break on the "and" reading, the address check unanchored, and scoring only the "and" reading; the alias tests still pass.
